title: Re-signing splits the forced dissonance and carries it anywhere
claim: Kasteleyn-signed knot spheres (two-coloured triangulations of the sphere). (1) In every state and law, violated lines minus over-agreement plus half the number of even faces is 1, so one sign change moves at most one unit between state and law, and with four or more even faces every state over-agrees. (2) On simplicial spheres every law with exactly two even faces is satisfiable wherever they sit (Euler's formula and Hall's theorem), so one sign change at the violated line always moves the dissonance out of the states, and every line is the violated line of some flat state. (3) Every line is the violated line of exactly 2 N(T) flat states, with N(T)^2 = det(B B^T)/(n0 n1 + n1 n2 + n2 n0) for B the line-face incidence matrix and n_i the colour classes of the vertex 3-colouring; two even faces of different colours never allow fewer than N(T) matchings, the value for adjacent faces (Kasteleyn's theorem, the 3-colouring kernel, complementary minors, Cauchy-Binet). (4) With the state held fixed, sign changes made only at the violated line or at an even face carry the dissonance from any line to any line through configurations holding only the forced unit, and a closed walk equals a block change of state.
failure_conditions: A simplicial two-coloured sphere with a pair of faces whose removal leaves the lines without a perfect matching.
Two lines of one sphere that are the violated lines of different numbers of flat states.

A start and target line that re-signings made only at the violated line or at an even face cannot connect with the state fixed, or an intermediate configuration holding more than the forced unit of dissonance.
foundation_claim_scope: Theorems 1-4 by proof for the stated spheres. Checked on the octahedral spheres K_2-K_8, two tubes, three grown spheres and four branched double covers.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-07.
validation.status: by hand, with the finite claims checked by computation with controls; no human or external review
validation.novelty: known-with-delta for theorems 1, 2 and 4 (Hall and Euler; COUNT-SURFACES-20261107-001A theorem 4; alternating paths, as in worm algorithms for dimers): the delta is the knot's law with its forced dissonance, read as learning. Theorem 3: no-overlap-found in a bounded search (uniform count over lines and its closed form); not a novelty claim.
